FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Machine Tool Elements and Holding Devices Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. The continuous research in the area of enhancing productivity has given rise to better machine tools and the efforts to reduce fatigue of workmen has led the development of workholding devices operated by power. The power operated chuck reduces the loading and unloading time and leads to higher productivity, by manually operated chucks. than achieved

This standard is one of a series of Indian Standard available on chucks. The other standards are as given below: IS No. 2876 : 1978 10612 : 1983 14725 : 1999 Title 3-jaw 4-jaw scroll operated self-centering 4-jaw independent lathe chucks V;rst revision)

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 2-JAW AND 3-JAW POWER OPERATED WEDGE TYPE CHUCKS - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies requirements for power operated self centering wedge type lathe chucks. 1.2 The chucks are of front mounting type that is chucks which are bolted from the front side of the chuck. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The following standards contain provision which through reference in this text, constitute provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the standards indicated below: IS No. 1570 : 1961 Title Schedules for wrought steels for general engineering purposes Acceptance code for machine tools-Geometric accuracy of machines operating under no-load or finishing conditions (first

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the terminology given below shall apply (see also Fig. 1). 3.1 Chuck Device to be mounted on the spindle nose of a machine tool for holding a work piece or a tool (directly or with an adapter). 3.2 Power Operated Self Centering Chucks as

A chuck in which all the jaws move simultaneously towards or away from the axis of rotation. This chuck is operated by hydraulic or pneumatic or electrical power actuator linked to chuck operating mechanism to move the jaws simultaneously inward or outward, radially to grip the work piece, concentric to the axis of rotation.

IS 14693 : 1999 3.3 Chuck Body The part ofthe chuck which encloses operating mechanisms, and jaws, and also provides for mounting. 3.3.i C'huck Fucc 6 DESIGNATION 6.1 A power operated 2-jaw and 3-jaw wedge type chuck shall be designated by name, number of jaws, nominal diameter and number of this standard. Example A power operated wedge type 2-jaw chuck of nominal dia 200 shall be designated as: Power Operated Chuck IS 14693-2-200 7 MOUNTING INSTRUCTIONS on the lathe

The face from which the master jaws protrude. 3.3.2 l3ai.k Fuce The face of chuck that contacts the face of the spindle or adaptor when chuck is mounted on the machine. 3.4 Master Jaw (Base Jaw)

The part formed to fit in the jaw slot ofthe chuck body and provides for mounting top jaw either hard or soft. Master jaws once fitted in a body shall not be interchanged. 3.5 Top Jaw 3.5.1 The work holding member, intended mounted and clamped on the master jaw. 3.5.2 The top jaw may be either hard or soft. 3.5.2,1 Hard jaws have to be ground in posiiion. Once so ground, the jaws shall not be interchanged. These jaws are reversible. 3.5.2.2 Soft jaws have to be machined in position. Once removed, these jaws have to be remachined after refitment. 3.6 Jaw Actuator This member of the chuck is connected to power source and moves the base jaw through chuck operating mechanism. 4 MATERIAL 4.1 Body Medium carbon steel having minimum hardness of 190 HB to 220 HB Jaw guide ways shall be hardened to 46 HRC to 52 HRC. 4.2 Master Jaw (Base Jaw) Suitable steel case hardened to a hardness of 54 1RC to 60 HRC. 4.3 Jaw Actuator (Wedge) Suitable steel case hardened to a hardness of 54 FIRC to 60 HRC. 5 DIMENSIONS 5.1 The dimensions Table 1. for chucks shall be as given in to be

7.1 The lathe chucks shall be mounted spindle as shown in Fig. 2. 8 TESTlNG 8. I Geometrical Test

8.1.1 Preliminary Remarks Since all the geometrical tests to be carried out involve the chuck rotation, the chuck should be mounted on the suitable test spindle. The mounting of the chuck on the spindle nose shall be made either directly on the spindle nose or with an adapter placed between the spindle nose and the chuck. The flange or the adaptor shall hav,e been already tested for the accuracy of size, concentricity with the spindle axis and absence of face out of the flange or adaptor. 8.1.2 Spindle Accuracy The spindle accuracy shall be tested according IS 2063 and 8.2.11 of iS 2876. 8.2 Concentricity of Outside Diameter to

When a chuck is mounted on spindle as shown in Fig. 2, the concentricity of the outside diameter shown by a dial indicator reading shall be within the limits as given in Table 3. 8.3 Accuracy of Grip on Test Bar The accuracy required shall be as given in Table 4. 8.3.1 This test shall be carried out with, mandrels of three different diameters as given in Table 4 for each size of chuck. The mandrel shall be clamped by jaws stepped outwards and the dial gauge shall be engaged on the mandrel at a distance `I' from the jaw. The dial gauge reading shall not exceed the maximum values given in Table 4. 8.3.2 The accuracy of test bar to be used shall conform to the requirements given in A-l of IS 2063. 8.4 Accuracy of Grip on Test Ring 8.4.1 External Jaws The accuracy of grip of external jaws on test ring shall be as given in Table 5. 2

5.2 The capacity of lathe chuck shall be as given in Table 2.

.Jaws

The accuracy of grip of internal jaws on test ring shall be as given in Table 6. 8.5 Static Balancing The static balance of the chuck shall be tested in the following manner. 8.5.1 The chuck shall be mounted on mandrel. The mandrel shall incorporate an adapter integral with it and accurately finished to fit the location of the chuck to be tested. The mandrel with the adaptor shall have been already balanced prior to the chuck being mounted on it. The

location of the cap screws, bolts or studs for holding the chuck on the adaptor shall be in balance. The chuck shall then be mounted on the adaptor and the mandrel placed on knife-edges as shown in Fig. 3. The weight required to effect the static balance for the self centering chuck shall conform to the limits specified in Table 7 and the arrangement is given in Fig. 3. The test shall be carried out only when the chuck is completely dry inside and without top jaws, T-nuts/ Hexagon socket cap screws. 9 RIGlDlTY The rigidity of a chuck shall be expressed in terms of its ability to reproduce its accuracy of grip on a test

9.1 The test shall be carried out as detailed below: a) The chucks shall be mounted on a lathe of adequate power and rigidity and a test bar shall be gripped in the jaws. The cutting test shall then be carried out at the feeds and depth of cut as specified in Table 8.

10.1 The chucks shall be given suitable sive surface treatment

10.2 The chuck shall be packed in accordance best trade practice. 11 MARKING

with

b)

The test bar shall be made of steel conforming to grade Cl4 of 1s 1570. Suitably heat treated to hardness of 20 HRC. The diameter of the test bar shall be equal to the maximum capacity of the chuck for bar work as specified by the manufacturer. The length of the test bar hanging out beyond the chuck jaw for this shall be twice the diameter of the bar. During the turning test the bar shall not be supported by any centre or steady rest. After completion of the test as specified in Table 8 the chuck shall be capable of retaining its original accuracy of grip as specified in 8.3 and 8.4.

c)
